profiles.name: Prototype pressure pipe
assumptions: All coordinates and linear dimensions are interpreted as millimeters for this prototype. The supplied drawing units have not been confirmed.
The 50 mm clearance is a chosen demo value. It is not a general industry standard or an organizer requirement.
Clearance is measured from the pipe outer surface to the modeled obstacle or routing boundary. Insulation is not included unless already represented in the input outer diameter.
The 250 mm grid spacing controls search resolution. It is not a physical pipe or fitting dimension.
Each direction change adds 300 mm to the search score. This is a preference used to compare routes and does not add to physical route length.
Connections and pipe outer diameter remain fixed. No hydraulic performance or material suitability is established by this profile.

profiles.name: Prototype gravity drain
assumptions: All coordinates and linear dimensions are interpreted as millimeters for this prototype. The supplied drawing units have not been confirmed.
The 50 mm clearance is a chosen demo value. It is not a general industry standard or an organizer requirement.
Clearance is measured from the pipe outer surface to the modeled obstacle or routing boundary. Insulation is not included unless already represented in the input outer diameter.
The 250 mm grid spacing and 300 mm bend penalty are search settings. They are not manufacturing dimensions.

The assumed minimum slope is 0.01 units of vertical fall per unit of horizontal travel. This is 1 percent or 10 mm per horizontal meter. It is a demo assumption rather than an approved drain requirement.
Flow is assumed to run from the input start connection to the end connection. Positive z is upward. The actual flow direction must be supplied correctly.
This profile records requirements for the prototype. A profile alone does not establish that every listed check or fitting is implemented.
Drain sizing and venting are not established by passing a geometric slope check.

notices: These profiles are editable prototype settings. They are not official ship rules or a declaration of standards compliance.
Changing a units label is not a unit conversion. When the source units are confirmed, convert all coordinates and linear dimensions consistently before running checks again.
Do not change the physical size of a source pipe to match an entry in this small fitting catalog. An unmatched diameter requires an appropriate fitting record or human review.
The catalog records do not establish an allowed material or pressure class for the challenge. They do not include fabrication tolerances or weld access allowances.
A centerline turn is not a complete fitting model. The full fitting envelope still needs a collision check before a route can be treated as buildable.
